deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred from pages 19-21). X = P^1 - {0,1,inf}, which is M_{0,4}. Its full automorphism group, holomorphic and antiholomorphic, is Gamma = S_3 x Z/2, where the Z/2 is complex conjugation. Fix the base point rho = e^{2 pi i/3}. Let pi = pi_1(X, rho), the free group on loops l_0, l_1, l_inf subject to the single relation (1) l_inf l_1 l_0 = 1. Let Sigma be the extension 1 -> pi -> Sigma -> Gamma -> 1, i.e. the orbifold fundamental group of X/Gamma. Concretely, Sigma is a copy of PGL_2(Z) containing pi = Gamma(2)/{±1}; the holomorphic part is PSL_2(Z).

The stabiliser of rho. On page 21 Grothendieck notes that the stabiliser of rho in Gamma is the 'anti-diagonal' copy phi(S_3) = {(s, sgn s)}. Transpositions act there as antiholomorphic reflections fixing rho and rho-bar. Because this stabiliser fixes the base point, it lifts canonically to a subgroup S~_3 of Sigma.

This page. It writes a presentation of the lift, (13):
- sigma~_i^2 = 1 for i = 0, 1, inf;
- sigma~_0 sigma~_1 = sigma~_1 sigma~_inf = sigma~_inf sigma~_0 = rho;
- rho^3 = 1 then follows, by multiplying the three equal products.

The preimage Sigma~ of phi(S_3) is the semidirect product pi x| S~_3. To make this explicit he computes the action (14). Each sigma~_i is a reflection fixing rho and rho-bar, so it reverses orientation and inverts loops: sigma~_0 sends l_0 -> l_0^{-1}, l_1 -> l_inf^{-1} and l_inf -> l_1^{-1}, and similarly for the other i.

Relations (13), (14) and (1) then give a presentation of Sigma~, an index-2 subgroup of Sigma (of PGL_2(Z)) other than PSL_2(Z); rho can be eliminated as a generator.

Finally he combines the holomorphic involutions sigma_i (from the earlier presentation of the holomorphic extension) with the sigma~_i, via (15) tau_i = sigma_i sigma~_i = sigma~_i sigma_i. Since the two commute, this gives (16) tau_i^2 = 1. These are three lifts to Sigma of complex conjugation (1, 1) in Gamma, presumably the reflections fixing the three real arcs (0,1), (1,inf), (inf,0). Page 21 calls them 'trois choix également naturels'.

The margin notes rho sigma_i rho^{-1} = sigma_{i+1} (cyclic permutation of 0 -> 1 -> inf). It also records a self-critique: these operations are not transports of structure, and a better normalisation of the relations between Sigma and Sigma~ is sought.

Purpose: an explicit, symmetric presentation of the extended modular / Teichmüller-type group of M_{0,4} including complex conjugation. This is groundwork for the Galois / Teichmüller-tower programme of 1981 and for comparing symmetric base points (rho, rho-bar, i) and real lifts.
errors: (13) checked: involutions a, b, c with ab = bc = ca generate a dihedral group of order 6, with (ab)^3 = 1 forced. So (13) presents S_3 correctly, and rho^3 = 1 is indeed a consequence.
(14) is consistent with (1): applying sigma~_0 to l_inf l_1 l_0 gives l_1^{-1} l_inf^{-1} l_0^{-1} = (l_0 l_inf l_1)^{-1}, a conjugate of 1.

The commutation sigma_i sigma~_i = sigma~_i sigma_i used in (15) is asserted without proof on this page. The holomorphic transpositions swap rho and rho-bar, so whether this holds depends on the conventions of the earlier pages for sigma_i; I could not verify it from this page alone.
The '...' in (14) leave the actions of sigma~_1 and sigma~_inf on the other loops unwritten. They are obtained by conjugating with rho, using the marginal NB.

ideas.what: Presentation of the stabiliser of the symmetric base point rho, inside the full (holomorphic plus antiholomorphic) automorphism group of P^1-{0,1,inf}, as three involutions with sigma~_0 sigma~_1 = sigma~_1 sigma~_inf = sigma~_inf sigma~_0 = rho.
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral vertex stabiliser of the (2,3,inf) extended triangle group, PGL_2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke; Coxeter presentation of PGL_2(Z))

ideas.what: Semidirect product decomposition pi_1(X, rho) x| S~_3, with explicit action of the reflections on the standard loops (inverting and swapping them).
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental group of M_{0,4}/(S_3 x Z/2); index-2 subgroup of PGL_2(Z) containing Gamma(2)/±1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical. In the GT context: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses M_{0,4}, its S_3 symmetries and the Teichmüller tower in general terms only

ideas.what: Three lifts tau_i of complex conjugation, each an involution, obtained as products of holomorphic and antiholomorphic involutions; read as reflections along the three real arcs.
ideas.modern_name: Lifts of complex conjugation to the profinite/discrete Teichmüller group; real points and tangential base points on real arcs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Nakamura; Lochak–Schneps; Pop (complex conjugation in GT-type groups)

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically incorporates complex conjugation (the Z/2 factor) into the symmetric presentation of the Teichmüller group of M_{0,4} as early as 1981. He uses the symmetric base point rho and notes that complex conjugation has three equally natural involutive lifts, tied to the three real arcs. This anticipates the later study of complex conjugation inside GT-type groups, but the mathematics itself is classical.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that the 'real' (Z/2) part of the Galois–Teichmüller picture was in Grothendieck's 1981 drafts, before Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak–Schneps. No new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, essentially routine computation of a presentation of an index-2 subgroup of PGL_2(Z) adapted to M_{0,4} with base point rho. It is of historical interest for the 1981 Teichmüller/Galois programme, including complex conjugation, but contains nothing absent from the later literature.
